posture: The quietest stretch of the reform rollout has broken, and it has broken on conduct rather than scheme design. SIRA issued a Letter of Censure to Aldi on 27 August under section 183A(1)(b) of the Workers Compensation Act 1987 for failing to meet claims and injury management standards under its self-insurer licence, after an independent audit in May 2026 found problems still open in areas that had been under remediation and enhanced supervision since 2023. That is the first named self-insurer censure this digest has recorded under the reformed regime, and SIRA has said explicitly that continued non-compliance may attract further regulatory action. It also closes a gap: the item was published on 27 August and the 28 August digest wrongly reported that SIRA's news channel had not moved past Bulletin Issue 77 of 18 August. Two days later the ABC published a multi-jurisdiction investigation into Gallagher Bassett, carrying allegations from injured workers in the NT, NSW and Victorian schemes about delayed treatment approvals and cut payments, and citing WorkSafe Victoria's 2024-25 agent scorecard placing the firm last on six-month return to work at 66.6%. Read together the two items point the same way: claims-handling performance, not premium or benefit design, is where scheme scrutiny is now landing. Elsewhere in NSW, SafeWork secured an $800,000 District Court penalty on 28 August over a 2022 reach stacker fatality, and the IRO relaunched its website on 27 August alongside an ILARS funding e-learning module and its 2025-26 annual performance review. APRA's June-quarter general insurance statistics landed on 27 August. AFR, SMH and Guardian Australia could not be checked this run because none of those domains is reachable by the search tool, so no paywalled items are captured and none are asserted. Interstate movement was routine only. NSW is now in week nine of the reformed regime and the scheme settings recorded since 28 June are unchanged: the 1.99% Nominal Insurer target collection rate frozen to 30 June 2028, industry classification rates held for 2026-27, the revised Workers Compensation Guidelines 2026 and 2026 Market Practice and Premium Guidelines in force, the 25% WPI threshold on primary psychological injury claims notified from 1 July 2026, the reasonable-and-necessary treatment test due 1 October 2026, and Megan Main due to take over as SIRA chief executive on 12 October.
summary: SIRA publicly censured Aldi's NSW self-insurer licence for sustained claims management failures, the first named self-insurer censure logged under the reformed regime and an explicit warning that further regulatory action is available. Two days later the ABC ran a multi-jurisdiction investigation into Gallagher Bassett's claims handling across the NT, NSW and Victorian schemes, naming WorkSafe Victoria's own scorecard as evidence. Supporting items: an $800,000 SafeWork NSW fatality penalty, the IRO's website and ILARS funding relaunch with its 2025-26 performance review, and APRA's June-quarter general insurance statistics.

items.headline: SIRA censures Aldi's NSW self-insurer licence after an audit found remediation issues still unresolved
items.summary: SIRA issued a Letter of Censure to Aldi Stores on 27 August under section 183A(1)(b) of the Workers Compensation Act 1987, finding it had contravened licence condition 4.1 by failing to manage claims and injury management to an acceptable standard. Aldi has been under enhanced regulatory oversight since 2023, and an independent audit in May 2026 found problems still open in areas already subject to remediation.
items.so_what: This is the first named self-insurer censure this digest has recorded under the reformed regime, and SIRA has said further action is available if compliance is not substantial and sustained. Self-insurers and claims service providers should read it as the regulator's current tolerance setting on claims handling performance and test their own audit findings against it now.

items.headline: ABC investigation gathers injured-worker allegations against Gallagher Bassett across three schemes
items.summary: The ABC reported allegations from injured workers and their lawyers that Gallagher Bassett delayed treatment approvals, reduced payments and declined to negotiate settlements, drawing on cases in the Northern Territory and referencing the firm's role managing claims for NT, NSW and Victorian public sector workers. The report cites WorkSafe Victoria's 2024-25 agent scorecard, which placed Gallagher Bassett last among Victorian agents on return to work within six months at 66.6%.
items.so_what: A claims service provider operating inside the NSW scheme is now carrying a national reputational story with a regulator's own performance metric attached, which raises the prospect of political and regulatory attention on agent conduct rather than benefit design. Risk functions should expect scrutiny of claims service provider oversight and escalation pathways, and should be able to evidence how agent performance is monitored.

items.headline: District Court fines container operator $800,000 over a 2022 fatality involving a reversing reach stacker
items.summary: SafeWork NSW announced on 28 August that a container services business was convicted and fined $800,000 in the NSW District Court after a defended hearing, over an April 2022 incident in which a pedestrian was fatally struck by a reversing reach stacker. The prosecution proceeded under the work health and safety duty owed to persons other than workers, and the company retains appeal rights.
items.so_what: The penalty is at the upper end of recent NSW outcomes and reinforces mobile plant as a stated SafeWork enforcement priority, which matters for premium-relevant exposure in logistics, warehousing and ports. Employers with pedestrian and mobile plant interaction should treat traffic management controls as an area regulators are actively testing in court.

items.headline: IRO relaunches its website and publishes an ILARS funding module alongside its 2025-26 performance review
items.summary: The Independent Review Office issued an alert on 27 August announcing a redesigned website with changed URLs, a new e-learning module for approved lawyers on navigating the ILARS funding guidelines, and the release of its annual performance review for July 2025 to June 2026. The module covers the ILARS Amending Instrument and the revised funding criteria that commenced on 1 July 2026, and an approved lawyer webinar is scheduled for 10 September.
items.so_what: The revised ILARS funding criteria shape which disputes get legally funded and therefore how dispute volumes move under the reformed regime, so the training push is a signal worth tracking rather than housekeeping. Anyone with bookmarked IRO references should also expect link breakage, and the annual review is the year's main published dataset on worker complaints about insurer conduct.

items.headline: APRA publishes June-quarter general insurance statistics, with employers' liability visible in the class breakdowns
items.summary: APRA released its quarterly general insurance performance statistics on 27 August, covering the June 2026 quarter and reporting a modest year-on-year fall in industry after-tax profit from continuing operations. The publication includes class of business and state level detail, which is where APRA-regulated employers' liability and workers compensation business shows up.
items.so_what: This is the periodic read on capital and class performance for the privately underwritten schemes in WA, Tasmania, the ACT and the Northern Territory, and for licensed insurers writing employers' liability nationally. It is scheduled data rather than an event, so treat it as the baseline against which any later solvency or pricing signal is judged; the next release is due in November.
